subject: math

objective.text: Arrange objects into an array with rows and columns. Count to find the total.

source_ref.section: Lesson objective

explanations.title: Rows make an array
explanations.text: A row goes straight across, left to right. Put equal groups into rows. The same number is in each row. This makes a rectangle called an array.

source_ref.section: Concept Development Problem 1 (rows)

explanations.title: Columns make an array
explanations.text: A column goes up and down. You can also put equal groups into columns. 2 columns of 3 looks like 2 rows of 3 turned sideways.

source_ref.section: Concept Development Problem 1 (columns)

explanations.title: The total stays the same
explanations.text: When you move objects into rows or columns, the total does not change. 6 bears stay 6 bears.

source_ref.section: Concept Development Problem 1 (Did the total change? No)

explanations.title: Count an array in different ways
explanations.text: Count one by one. Count row by row. Count column by column. Or skip-count. For 3 rows of 2, count 2, 4, 6.

source_ref.section: Concept Development Problem 1 (count by rows and columns)

explanations.title: One total, more than one array
explanations.text: 6 objects can be 1 group of 6, or 6 groups of 1. They can be 3 groups of 2, or 2 groups of 3. 12 beans can make 2 rows of 6.

assets_required.why_this_method: Exact object counts in rows and columns and switching between groups, rows and columns need exact behaviour. Diffusion cannot count.
assets_required.description: A board of identical objects (bears, beans or triangles). Objects can be shown as scattered groups, as rows, or as columns.
must_show_exactly: Exactly the object count in the stimulus
Every row has the same number of objects
Every column has the same number of objects
Rows go across, columns go up and down
states_or_frames: 6 bears as 1 group of 6, 6 groups of 1
4 rows of 5, 5 rows of 4, 2 rows of 10, 10 rows of 2 (20)
assets_required.interaction: Tutor sets the layout from the stimulus. Child can switch between groups, rows and columns. Child answers by voice or typing.
assets_required.alt_text: Objects arranged in neat rows and columns.
assets_required.generation_caption: Flat cartoon counting bears (or beans) arranged in an exact grid of rows and columns, plain background. [Build by code]
assets_required.review_notes: Use one original bear icon. Do not copy the source pictures.

visual_generation_rules: Diffusion cannot count reliably. Any picture where an exact number of objects matters must be built by code (SVG or widget) or drawn by an artist.
Diffusion is allowed only for: style or background art, and single icons (one ball, one pencil, one leaf, one character) that code then tiles to the exact count.
Every visual must be checked by a person: the count shown must equal the stimulus in the question and the rubric answer key.
Animations are described as frames with exact counts per frame, so they can be built or generated and then checked frame by frame.
Visual explanations are valid only when the asset exists (pipeline doc, Planner rules).
